edges.effect_quant: Dose-response evidence shows silicosis risk rises with cumulative respirable crystalline silica exposure, with mining and engineered-stone settings carrying especially high progression risk.
edges.population: workers with chronic occupational respirable crystalline silica exposure
edges.mechanism: Respirable crystalline silica is directly toxic to alveolar macrophages and drives a self-sustaining fibrotic cascade in the lung. Once cumulative exposure is high enough, the biology fits an exposure-dependent pneumoconiosis model much more than a subtle associative signal.
edges.summary: The best anchor is the recent dose-response meta-analysis showing that higher cumulative silica exposure maps to higher silicosis risk rather than merely correlating with dusty jobs in general. Other systematic reviews and cohort follow-up in rapidly progressive artificial-stone disease reinforce that this is one of the cleaner occupational harm edges in the graph.
edges.caveats: Absolute risk depends heavily on dust intensity, duration, and the silica content of the material being worked. Engineered-stone cohorts can progress faster than traditional mining cohorts, so they should not be treated as identical exposure settings.

evidence.notes: Relationship between cumulative silica exposure and silicosis: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis.
